messages:
alex_h: FYI we started seeing a ~2x p99 jump for text-generation in syd POP around 09:04 UTC. Spike correlates with a burst of KV cache evictions and elevated retransmits on the egress link. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/s/dash/syd-pop-latency
jenna_s: I see it in traces too — tail latency moved from ~120ms -> ~260ms. Anything recent deployed? :thinking_face:
alex_h: small rollout 09:00 — runtime kernel selection tweak (auto-fallback) and a batching heuristic change (batching.threshold lowered). I rolled back batching change at 09:12 but p99 stayed high.
maria_r: dump from runtime profiler (09:10):
```
kernel_selector: metrics:
  avx_fused: 48%
  fallback_mv: 47%
  osc_times: 23 switches/min
kv_cache: evictions/sec: 420 -> baseline 12
batch_avg_size: 6 -> 14
request_latency_p99: 120ms -> 260ms
```
maria_r: selector is oscillating between kernels which lines up with perf cliffs when context lengths vary. Frequent kernel swaps + higher batch sizes = more memory pressure -> KV evictions.
tim_ops: Network side: I pulled sflow/ifstats on the POP egress (09:05-09:15). Saw bursty tx queues and some retransmit spikes. Suspect bufferbloat at provider link. Snippet:
```
09:06:12 if_tx_queue_len=512 -> drop: 34
09:06:14 retransmits/sec: 120
09:07:00 if_qdisc: pfifo_fast backlog=1500
```
network_team_bot: Notified infra-networking channel. Provider (telco-xyz) shows increased output queue delay on their metro aggregation for SYD-1.
jenna_s: So we have two amplifiers: (1) bufferbloat causing PCR and higher RTT which increases in-flight tokens; (2) runtime oscillation and larger batches causing KV thrash. Both produce p99 spike.
alex_h: Agree. Quick mitigation plan proposed:
  - pin kernel_selector to stable kernel (avx_fused) for SYD POP (hotfix)
  - temporarily reduce max_batch_size to 8 for SYD to lower memory pressure
  - bump KV cache reservation for SYD hosts by 30% (config flag)
  - ask network to open ticket with provider for QoS / qdisc tuning
maria_r: I can push the kernel pin with a gated rollout to just syd that avoids global impact. Command:
```
# pin kernel selector
redwoodctl runtime set-config --pop syd --kernel pin:avx_fused --reason "mitigate oscillation during egress queueing"
```
deploy-bot: deployment queued: runtime-config-syd-pin (owner: maria_r) — ETA ~2m
tim_ops: network ticket opened with provider. They acknowledge potential bufferbloat, asked for pcap (I shared tcpdump sample). Provider scheduled probe.
jenna_s: After kernel pin + batch cap (09:18) I see p99 drop from 260ms -> 140ms. Still above baseline but better. KV evictions down from 420 -> 60/s.
alex_h: Good. Can you paste the profiler snapshot post-fix?
maria_r: post-fix 09:25:
```
kernel_selector: avx_fused: 99%
kv_cache evictions/sec: 60
batch_avg_size: 8
p99: 132ms
```
tim_ops: Provider applied qdisc adjustments at 09:30; links show tx queue delay decreased ~70% and retransmits returned to baseline. p99 after provider fix ~118ms (almost baseline).
jenna_s: Notes for follow-up (action items):
  - Instrument kernel selector to produce a short-term metric: switches/min per host (alert if >5/min)
  - Add backpressure to batching heuristic when RTT increases >30ms relative to host baseline
  - Increase default KV reservation in POPs that have 95th percentile load > X
  - Postmortem to document the cross-layer amplification (network qdisc + runtime oscillation)
alex_h: I'll own the postmortem. Quick TODOs assigned: kernel selector metric (maria_r), batching backpressure (jenna_s), KV reservation policy update (alex_h), network follow-up (tim_ops).
maria_r: adding a short-lived dashboard panel for kernel-switch-rate + kv-evictions per-host.
jenna_s: Thanks all. Good catch on the provider side too — that was the multiplier.
alex_h: Closing thread once postmortem is up. :thumbsup:
